blocks.text: Dear Mr. Keller:

This letter sets down the terms on which our firm will undertake the working capital program we have discussed with you, and, once you have signed the enclosed copy and returned it to me, it will stand as the agreement between us and {{fact:f:E-2013-001.client}}. I have written it plainly, and at more length than a shorter note would take, because I would rather we understand one another fully at the outset than leave anything of consequence to be settled once the work is already running; I would ask you to read it against the conversations we have had and to tell me, before you sign, of anything in it that does not answer to how you remember them.
What the Engagement Covers

We will help {{fact:f:E-2013-001.client}} find and release the cash that is presently tied up in the ordinary running of the business, working through the three places such cash usually sits: the money owed to you by your customers, the money you owe your suppliers, and the value held in inventory. Our aim is a practical program that frees working capital without straining the relationships and service levels the business depends upon, and so our recommendations will be weighed as much for what they cost the organization to carry out as for what they promise to return. The engagement is advisory. The decisions it informs remain yours, and where our work touches questions of accounting, tax, or law you should continue to rely on the advisers who ordinarily provide that counsel, since what we offer on such matters is a considered view and not a professional opinion in their place.
How We Intend to Proceed

We will begin by understanding how cash moves through {{fact:f:E-2013-001.client}} as it stands today, drawing on your own records and on a short round of conversations with the people who manage collections, payments, and stock, before we commit any recommendation to paper. Only once we and your team agree the present picture will we set out the changes worth making, and we will order those changes so that the organization can absorb them without losing a step. Where the ground shifts under the work, as it commonly does once real numbers come in, we will bring the revised plan back to you rather than press on around it.
The People Who Will Carry It

Jason Torres, a Principal of the firm, will lead the engagement from day to day and will be the person to whom you bring any question of substance; he is accustomed to telling a client what the figures show rather than what is most comfortable to hear, and you should expect that of him. Brenda Rodriguez, a Senior Consultant, will carry the analytical core of the work and is careful about what a number can and cannot be made to say, and John Vasquez will assemble and reconcile the underlying data so that any figure we place before you can be traced back to where it came from. I will keep my own hand on the engagement at the points where a judgment must be made about how far a conclusion can be pressed before it outruns what we actually know, and nothing of consequence will leave the firm under our name without my having read it first.
Fee and Payment

Our fee for the engagement as I have described it is {{fact:f:E-2013-001.fee}}, which covers the time of the people named above through the expected close of the work. We will render invoices against that amount as the work proceeds, and each will be payable within thirty days of your receipt of it. The fee covers our people and their time and not the incidental costs of the work, such as travel or the reproduction of materials, which we will incur only with your agreement and pass through to you at what they cost us; should the shape of the work change materially from what this letter contemplates, I will raise the question of the fee with you and we will settle it together before any further work begins, so that nothing reaches you on an invoice as a surprise.
When the Work Begins and How It May End

The engagement will begin on {{fact:f:E-2013-001.start}} and is expected to run for something on the order of seven months, though we will treat it as complete when the work is genuinely done and not merely when the calendar has turned. Either of us may bring it to an end on fourteen days' written notice to the other; should you choose to do so, you will owe us for the work properly performed to that point and for any costs already committed on your behalf, and for nothing beyond that.
Confidential Information

Everything we learn about {{fact:f:E-2013-001.client}} in the course of this work we will hold in confidence and use only for the purposes of the engagement. That obligation binds every member of the team, it survives the end of our work, and it covers the fact of our involvement as fully as it covers its substance. We ask the same of you in respect of the methods and written materials we share with you, which represent the firm's own way of working.
The Limit of Our Responsibility

We will perform the work with the care and skill you are entitled to expect of a firm engaged for it, and we stand behind what we do. We do not, however, control the decisions your management will ultimately take, nor the conditions of the markets and the suppliers and customers with whom you deal, and so, save to the extent the law does not permit such a limit, our liability to you arising out of this engagement is limited to the fees paid under it.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which our firm is established, and any dispute arising under it will be determined by the courts of that state. Should any single provision of this letter be held unenforceable, the remainder of it will continue in force, unaffected.

If this letter states our understanding correctly, I would be grateful if you would sign the enclosed copy where indicated below and return it to me, keeping the other for your own file. Once your signed copy is in our hands, John Vasquez will write to arrange the first requests for information and the opening working sessions, so that we can begin without delay. I look forward to the work.
